Subject: Post-call — Path to Pilot & operational questions (BlueArc Health)

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciate the candid conversation. Below is a concise recap, the suggested pilot scope, owners, and a short list of operational items we need to kick off. I call out the open questions we discussed so we can align before the kickoff.

Quick recap of pain points you shared:
- Production latency variability on peak business hours (~300–800ms P95 currently) causing poor triage experience for clinicians.
- High per-call cost driven by long context windows and frequent model reloads.
- Concern about PHI handling, audit logs, and vendor access controls for PII.

Primary goals for the pilot (agreed):
1) Validate 200ms P95 chat latency with a realistic prompt set (70–120 token responses).
2) Reduce per-session inference cost by at least 25% using batching + prefix caching and a quantized model variant.
3) Demonstrate secure setup for PHI-sensitive requests: VPC peering, KMS-managed keys, plus audit log retention for 90 days.

Proposed pilot scope (2–3 weeks active evaluation):
- Workload: triage assistant prompts (we'll use the sample prompt_eval_sample.jsonl attached).
- Metrics: 95th percentile latency (ms), cost per 1k tokens (USD), and mean correctness on 50 fixed eval prompts (you'll see the eval matrix in the PDF).
- Deliverables: runbook with access instructions, weekly telemetry snapshot, final evaluation report with recommendations.

Owners / contacts:
- Redwood lead: Naomi Feldman (pilot PM) — naomi@redwood.com
- Redwood technical lead: Jasmine Liu (runtime/observability) — jasmine_liu@redwood.com
- BlueArc product: Susan Park — susan@bluearchealth.com
- BlueArc infra: Michael Torres — michael.t@bluearchealth.com

Immediate operational asks from BlueArc (items we agreed on for the kickoff):
1) Provide a test dataset (anonymized) or a 100–200 prompt sample we can run in the eval harness.
2) Add a service account with S3 read access for logs + a destination bucket for telemetry (we'll provide a policy).
3) Confirm whether you need SSO/SCIM before provisioning (we support SAML + OIDC; details below).
4) Network: allow the egress ranges in network_egress_ranges.xlsx and confirm whether a dedicated proxy is required.

Open questions we need answered before we start:
- Is SOC2 type II evidence required for vendor onboarding? If yes, will your security team accept our SOC2 report (link below) or do you need additional artifacts?
- Expected business hours for the trial traffic (so we can align load profile).

Attachments included: redwood_poc_scope_v1.pdf (scope + eval plan), prompt_eval_sample.jsonl, network_egress_ranges.xlsx.

Proposed kickoff window: Tue 30 Nov — Thu 2 Dec. Naomi will own scheduling and the first-day walkthrough. If that works, I'll send calendar invites and a short agenda.

Next step: Susan — can you confirm the test-data availability and whether security needs the SOC2 before the kickoff?

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
